unit.title: Two of you: the planner and the impulse
unit.needIt: You plan to study and end up on your phone. Knowing you are both a planner and a creature of impulse is the first step to managing either.
unit.why: The lecture introduces a course that blends old philosophy with modern science. It looks at humans as both smart thinkers who can plan for the future and as animals driven by instincts we cannot always control.
unit.outcome: Understand the mix of reason and instinct that shapes human behavior.
unit.reachesYou: You see this when you struggle to stay focused on a goal despite knowing you should. You also feel it when you have to make a split-second choice in a stressful situation.
unit.do: Identify one thing you want to do but keep putting off. Think of one way to make it harder to get distracted by your phone.

quiz.q: What two fields are combined in this course title?
quiz.why: The lecture states the course is listed in both philosophy and cognitive science.
quiz.quote: It's called Philosophy and the Science of Human Nature, and it's listed both in philosophy and in cognitive science.

quiz.q: What is one of the three main ethical theories covered?
quiz.why: Utilitarianism is listed as one of the three main ethical theories.
quiz.quote: We'll talk about utilitarianism, we'll talk about deontology, and we'll talk about virtue ethics, and we'll talk about how those relate to one another.

quiz.q: Which philosopher's work on the state is mentioned?
quiz.why: The lecturer mentions looking at the work of Thomas Hobbes on the state.
quiz.quote: We'll very briefly look at the work of Thomas Hobbes on the legitimacy of the state.

quiz.q: What is the main goal of the course regarding the different fields of study?
choices: To provide a coherent story about what human beings are
To teach every single fact from every field
To focus only on the history of philosophy
To teach students how to become professional scientists
quiz.why: The lecturer states the goal is to bring the fields together to tell a story about human nature.
quiz.quote: So what I'm going to try to do in the course is to bring together these eight fields in a way that provides a coherent story about what kind of thing human beings are and how we can learn about what kind of things human beings are from these various perspectives.

quiz.q: What does the lecture say about the 'soul' in ancient philosophy?
choices: It is the only thing that matters for happiness
It is a physical organ in the brain
It thrives when its parts are in harmony
It is something that science cannot measure
quiz.why: The lecture explains that ancient philosophers believed humans thrive when their souls are well-ordered.
quiz.quote: It turns out that the ancient philosophers' answer to that question is that human beings thrive when their souls are well-ordered, to use the ancient metaphor.

quiz.q: What is the main idea of the Ring of Gyges?
choices: People only act justly because they fear punishment
quiz.why: Glaucon argues that people only act justly because they lack the power to do injustice.
quiz.quote: Glaucon's conclusion from this story is that those who practice justice, those who act in conformity with the moral code of their society, do so because they lack the power to do injustice.

quiz.q: What is the 'ICE' credit card solution?
choices: Putting a card in a freezer
quiz.why: The lecture describes putting a credit card in a glass of water in the freezer.
quiz.quote: Dan Ariely describes an example of what he calls the ICE credit card solution, where if you have a tendency to make impulse purchases on the internet, you take your credit card and you put it put it in a glass of water, which you put into the freezer.

partials: We can plan for the long term.
We often give in to immediate urges.
We can use strategies to manage these urges.
crystal.key: Human nature is a mix of rational planning and non-rational impulses.

decoys.why: The lecture says we are also subject to forces beyond our rational control.

decoys.text: Procrastination is a lack of intelligence.
decoys.why: The lecture treats it as a conflict between different parts of our nature.

crystal.aha: By understanding both our rational and impulsive sides, we can better design our lives and societies.

scene.analogy: A shopping list and the snack aisle

actors.label: You wrote the list. You also filled the cart.

beats.say: You walk in with a list.
Then you pass the snack aisle.
The list says what you meant to buy.

right.sub: what ends up in the cart

beats.say: The cart shows what you did.
This course asks how those two parts of you can live together.
